I'd like to add column with clickable urls to my table and display it.
So in my server.R I have

http_url <- "http://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/directLink.do?

for(i in 1:length(ind_order)){

after running my application, a space between "<" and "a" appears, so
instead of url the following is displayed

http_url <- "http://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/directLink.do?experimentAccessionNumber="
    
    for(i in 1:length(ind_order)){

acc_numbers_cl[i] = paste0("<a href=\"",paste0(http_url,acc_num[ind_order][i]),"\">",acc_num[ind_order][i],"</a>") 
    }
    
    Cos_dist=distMatr[ind_order,ind]
   
    num_pep_ind=num_pep[ind_order]
    matr<-cbind(acc_numbers_cl,Cos_dist,num_pep_ind)
    colnames(matr)<-c("Accession numbers of closest experiments","Cosine similarity","Number of peptides in exp")
    matr
  })
  
})

messages.subject: Re: problems with displaying href in table
parts:
I think the problem is that the xtable() function (which converts the object to an HTML table) won't write the raw HTML, which you are trying to do with the <a href> stuff.

One way to do this is to write out the entire table yourself in html, and use htmlOutput() in the UI. Here's an example of generating a simple table. Note that this uses the shinyRun() function that I just posted a message about -- you should be able to simply copy and paste this code into your R session, and it will run the example:

# Install downloader the first time
install.packages('downloader')

downloader::source_url("https://gist.github.com/wch/5003044/raw/aa4dbbca0023e29a629386b1ee9a5d27b2e37362/shinyserialize.r")

shinyRun(
#--------------------------------------------------------------
`server.R` = quote({
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$test_table <- reactiveText(function() {

        str <- "<table border=1>\n"
        for (i in 1:input$n) {
          str <- paste(str, "  <tr>\n", sep = "")
          for (j in 1:input$n) {
            str <- paste(str, "    <td>", i, ":", j, "</td>", sep = "")
          }
        }
        str
    })
})
}),
#--------------------------------------------------------------
`ui.R` = quote({
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("HTML output"), 
  sidebarPanel(sliderInput("n", 
    "Number of on each side:", min = 0, max = 10, value = 5)), 
    mainPanel(htmlOutput("test_table"))
))
})
)

-Winston

parts:
I have gotten around this with some of the extensions of renderTable such as FooTable by doing this adding this as a parameter to xtable:

sanitize.text.function = function(x){x}

This stops xtable from pulling out the html stuff but probably opens it up to possible errors.

I'm not sure how to achieve this with the default renderTable in shiny.

On Thursday, February 21, 2013 5:27:51 PM UTC, Winston Chang wrote:
I think the problem is that the xtable() function (which converts the object to an HTML table) won't write the raw HTML, which you are trying to do with the <a href> stuff.

One way to do this is to write out the entire table yourself in html, and use htmlOutput() in the UI. Here's an example of generating a simple table. Note that this uses the shinyRun() function that I just posted a message about -- you should be able to simply copy and paste this code into your R session, and it will run the example:

# Install downloader the first time
install.packages('downloader')

downloader::source_url("https://gist.github.com/wch/5003044/raw/aa4dbbca0023e29a629386b1ee9a5d27b2e37362/shinyserialize.r")

shinyRun(
#--------------------------------------------------------------
`server.R` = quote({
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$test_table <- reactiveText(function() {

        str <- "<table border=1>\n"
        for (i in 1:input$n) {
          str <- paste(str, "  <tr>\n", sep = "")
          for (j in 1:input$n) {
            str <- paste(str, "    <td>", i, ":", j, "</td>", sep = "")
          }
        }
        str
    })
})
}),
#--------------------------------------------------------------
`ui.R` = quote({
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("HTML output"), 
  sidebarPanel(sliderInput("n", 
    "Number of on each side:", min = 0, max = 10, value = 5)), 
    mainPanel(htmlOutput("test_table"))
))
})
)

-Winston
